scenes.title: Photosynthesis
scenes.narration: Every second, the green plants around you are quietly performing one of the most important chemical reactions on Earth: photosynthesis. Let's see how it works.

data.subtitle: How plants turn sunlight into food

scenes.title: The Big Picture
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis happens in tiny green structures called chloroplasts. The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air, and water from the soil. Using energy from sunlight, it transforms them into glucose, its food, and releases oxygen, the very air we breathe.

scenes.title: Two Stages
scenes.narration: The process has two stages. First, the light reactions: chlorophyll captures sunlight and splits water molecules, releasing oxygen and storing energy. Second, the Calvin cycle: using that stored energy, the plant fixes carbon dioxide and builds glucose.

steps: Light reactions: chlorophyll captures sunlight, splits H₂O → O₂ + energy
Calvin cycle: uses stored energy to fix CO₂ → glucose

scenes.title: Why It Matters
scenes.narration: So remember this: photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy, produces nearly all the oxygen in our atmosphere, and feeds almost every food chain on the planet. One simple equation, powering nearly all life on Earth.

bullets: Foundation of nearly all food chains
